subject.title: [Data] Quality signals for ClawHub Skills — we analyzed the top 50 and found trust gaps

question: Should ClawHub add public multidimensional skill-quality signals, and should this issue's top-50 static-analysis dataset influence that scoring model or remain discussion input only?
rationale: The remaining work changes marketplace trust semantics, author reputation signals, and possibly discovery or install behavior, so automation cannot safely choose the scoring authority, public meaning, data handling, or appeal model.

options.title: Fold into a quality-signal RFC
options.body: Keep this issue open or link it from a canonical RFC so the dataset informs dimensions without making the external analyzer authoritative.

options.title: Adopt a narrow advisory score
options.body: Define a non-enforcement score with clear provenance, freshness, and no ranking/install effect until maintainers validate the model.

options.title: Keep scoring internal for now
options.body: Use the data for research and moderation discussion without exposing a public quality badge until maintainers are ready to own false positives and appeals.

recommendation.title: Fold into a quality-signal RFC
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open or link it from a canonical RFC so the dataset informs dimensions without making the external analyzer authoritative.

likelyOwner.reason: Patrick-Erichsen is CODEOWNERS-listed on the backend/security paths and authored the current quality-gate lines, making them the best available routing owner for this policy choice.
